Consult Summary:
45-year-old woman with SLE on methotrexate presents with one-day history of right-sided pleuritic pain, mild haemoptysis, subjective fever and shortness of breath on a two-week background of fatigue; remote video examination acceptable but inconclusive. GP suspects acute chest infection/pneumonia; face-to-face review arranged today for physical examination and possible antibiotics.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute respiratory illness (suspected chest infection / pneumonia)
- Onset: sudden today.
- Symptoms: right-sided back pain on deep inspiration, two episodes of coughing up blood, subjective fever, shortness of breath; palpitations but pulse 66–74 bpm when counted; no recent long-haul travel; no personal/family history of thromboembolism.
- Pertinent negatives: non-smoker; no known drug or other allergies.
- Examination (remote): stable appearance, pulse 66–74 bpm, capillary refill normal, oropharynx visually unremarkable, no cervical lymphadenopathy. No auscultation or vitals (BP, SpO₂, temp) obtained.
- Impression: likely lower respiratory tract infection; differentials include pulmonary embolism, pleurisy, malignancy.
- Plan: same-day in-person GP review for chest auscultation, vitals, consider chest X-ray and bloods; commence antibiotics if clinically indicated; safety-net advice given.

Issue 2: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
- Stable; managed with methotrexate (took dose this morning).
- Relevance: immunosuppression may predispose to infection and modify presentation.

Issue 3: Health anxiety regarding lung cancer
- Patient expressed fear that haemoptysis represents lung cancer.
- Reassured that acute presentation more consistent with infection; possible imaging pending clinical course.

Medications:
- Methotrexate – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- No known drug or other allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.

Social History:
- Lives alone in a flat; owns a cat.
- Occupation: office desk job.
- Smoking: never smoker.
- Alcohol: not discussed.

Preventative History:
- No information provided on screening tests or vaccinations.

Physical Examination:
- Pulse (self-counted): ~66–74 bpm.
- Capillary refill: brisk.
- Throat: normal visualisation.
- Cervical lymph nodes: not enlarged per patient palpation.
- Other vitals (BP, temperature, respiratory rate, SpO₂) not obtained.

Plan:
- Arrange same-day face-to-face GP appointment for chest examination, vital signs, and further assessment.
- If bacterial infection confirmed, commence appropriate antibiotic (no drug allergies reported).
- Consider chest X-ray and further investigations if clinical findings warrant or if symptoms persist.
- Monitor for worsening breathlessness, increased haemoptysis, high fever; attend emergency services if deterioration.
- Provide support team contact number for appointment coordination.
- Review methotrexate use and recent blood monitoring at follow-up.

Quality checks (document_quality):

● Missing expected elements:
  - Objective temperature, BP, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation.
  - Detailed methotrexate dose, frequency, recent blood test results.
  - Comprehensive medication reconciliation (only methotrexate discussed).
  - Alcohol intake, vaccination and cancer screening history.

● Internal conflicts:
  - Patient gave name as Tracy Chapman initially, later identified as “Doris” (conflict noted).
  - Age stated as “forty five” but exact DOB not provided.

● Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; occasional minor inaudible segments but clinical content understandable.
